reasons: Lake identity verifies United States v. Conner as the input case name, with expected citation found and party text/canonical-name matches.

defect.evidence_quote: The officers stayed in the motel room to secure the evidence but did not conduct a search of the room until they obtained a warrant.
defect.locator_note: content_page.md homes frontmatter and Appears on entry
defect.problem: The disclosed evidence supports a connection to officers securing a motel room after entry, but it does not disclose the Securing the Scene home taxonomy or any basis for the role label Recent development (role-based).
defect.proposed_fix: Either provide the Securing the Scene home-role criteria in the disclosed evidence or downgrade the role to a narrower, evidence-backed label tied to warrantless motel-room entry/securing evidence after illegal entry.

reasons: The opinion text contains a securing-the-evidence fact, but no disclosed file defines why this 1997 case is a Recent development or what role-based means.
Defaulting to refuted because the classification cannot be verified from the disclosed corpus files.
residual_risks: The classification may be correct under an undisclosed home-page taxonomy.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add disclosed taxonomy support for the home role or use a descriptive role such as coerced motel-room entry after demand to open door.

defect.evidence_quote: an unconstitutional search occurs when officers gain visual or physical access to a motel room after an occupant opens the door not voluntarily, but in response to a demand under color of authority.
defect.problem: The frontmatter holding is truncated and ends with 'not...', so the assertion as framed does not state a complete holding.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace the truncated holding with: Where officers gain visual or physical access to a motel room after an occupant opens the door not voluntarily, but in response to a demand under color of authority, the access is an unconstitutional search/intrusion absent consent or exigency.

reasons: The opinion text at the 666 page marker supports the complete rule, but the content_page holding field is visibly incomplete.
The page's Rule section contains a faithful complete quote, showing the holding can be repaired from disclosed evidence.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use the complete quoted rule from the opinion as the holding summary, with factual limits to motel-room visual/physical access after a demand under color of authority.

reasons: Lens A does not audit treatment/currentness, and I raise no treatment finding.

residual_risks: Binding-effect semantics were not independently audited under Lens A.
